name: Refugee Status (CONARE)

qualifying_event.description: A person with a well-founded fear of persecution, or fleeing generalized violence, foreign aggression, internal conflict, or massive human rights violations, may apply for refugee status.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Verbal or written application to CONARE's Executive Secretariat; personal interview.

requirements.blocker_text: Well-founded fear of persecution based on race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group, or political opinion.
Life, security, or liberty threatened by generalized violence, foreign aggression, internal conflict, or massive human rights violations in the country of origin.

evidence_required.document: Written or verbal application to CONARE's Executive Secretariat

outcome.duration_length: Provisional residence certificate issued within 20 business days; work-authorized documentation within 30 days of recognition

sources.title: República Argentina -- Ley 26.165, Ley General de Reconocimiento y Protección al Refugiado: CONARE composition and decision process, refugee definition (persecution and generalized-violence grounds), 20-business-day provisional certificate, 30-day work authorization, appeal to the Interior Minister within 10 days

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Argentina). Unusually favorable outcome relative to most humanitarian routes in this dataset: recognized refugees get full work rights within 30 days and access to basic humanitarian assistance (housing, food, health, education) while the claim is pending, per the law's explicit text. citizenship_after_months (24) reflects that recognized refugees appear to access the same standalone 2-year Ley 346 naturalization clock as any other legal resident (see ar_naturalisation.json and ar_permanent_residence.json, which notes refugees with sufficient territorial attachment can also access permanent residence directly) -- no refugee-specific accelerated citizenship timeline was found stated in this pass, so this is the general-route figure, not a refugee-specific one. Decision body: CONARE (5 commissioners: Interior, Foreign Affairs, Justice/Human Rights, Social Development, National Institute Against Discrimination), two-thirds quorum, simple-majority decision; appeal to the Interior Minister within 10 days of notification.
